label: copy-phase input c (fed back), not the first recalled token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input token is the letter c (100% of activations have in_tok == c; it never fires in the original or delimiter phase, or on any other token). It is almost silent when c is the first original token being echoed back (recall_idx 1), so the predicate requires recall_idx >= 2. Strongest activations come when c sits at original positions 2-3 and is followed by another c (the second c of a cc pair fires about half as strongly). It does not fire on c during the original phase. About 18% of copy-phase c inputs with recall_idx >= 2 stay inactive, so precision is incomplete; positional modulation inside the copy phase is weak (rate roughly flat for recall_idx 3-8).

issues: The test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.819, R 0.985, F1 0.894, mass recall 0.994. The plain rule (phase == 2) & (in_tok == c) also checks out on test, with recall 1.0, precision 0.677 and F1 0.807. Every activation has in_tok == c and phase == 2, and there are none in the original or delimiter phase (from the profile).

The 18% of predicted steps that stay inactive are not spread evenly. Test precision by recall_idx: 1 = 0.05, 2 = 0.61, 3 = 0.93, 4 = 0.91, 5 = 0.83, 6 = 0.82, 7 = 0.85, 8 = 0.80. So about 39% of c inputs at recall_idx 2 (c at original position 1) are silent, against 7-20% elsewhere. The explanation's 'roughly flat for recall_idx 3-8' is fair, but it should say the non-firing is concentrated at recall_idx 2.

At recall_idx 2, firing depends on the first original token in a graded, idiosyncratic way (dev precision). Strong first tokens are p/3/g/x/h/i/o, at 0.81-0.90. Weak ones are c/a/w/j/y/0/n/k, at 0.32-0.46. Gating recall_idx 2 on a first-token set ghilmoprtx23 raises test precision to 0.870 but drops recall to 0.906, for F1 0.887, so it does not beat the reported predicate. I treat this as modulation, not a clean counterexample class.

The cc-pair claim mostly holds. Test precision for c with prev_tok == c is 0.74 at recall_idx >= 3 and 0.34 at recall_idx 2, and the top examples show the second c at roughly 0.15-0.65 of the first. Excluding prev_tok == c lowers F1 (0.887).

The test misses are the recall_idx 1 cases (c as first token, weak activations of about 0.01-0.22, 0.6% of mass) plus one second c of a cc pair. That is consistent with 'almost silent' at recall_idx 1.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
